content.title: About
content.content: Vegetarian Gravy is a thick, aromatic sauce made from vegetable broth, plant-based fats, and spices. It is designed to accompany potatoes, vegetables, vegetarian patties and other dishes as a plant‑based alternative to traditional meat gravy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Vegetarian gravy is often based on mushroom broth, which gives it a characteristic "meaty" flavor.
There are many variations: with soy sauce, tomato paste, smoked spices, etc.
The sauce keeps well in the refrigerator for up to 7 days and can be frozen for up to 3 months.
While classic recipes use flour for thickening, vegetarian versions frequently use corn starch or tapioca.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Contains protein from soy or pea ingredients, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Plant oils such as rapeseed oil provide mostly polyunsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Provides vitamin B6 and niacin, which aid metabolic processes.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and spices like rosemary and thyme have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetable broth helps maintain normal gastrointestinal function.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: If the gravy contains soy protein, individuals with soy allergy may experience reactions.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared gravy can be salty; people monitoring sodium intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional thickener is wheat flour; choose a gluten‑free version if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the gravy gently to a light simmer and pour over mashed potatoes, roasted vegetables, vegetarian patties or burgers. It can also be stirred into stews for a richer consistency.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 7 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size containers for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
